title: partner-channel-friction-matrix-and-snippet-kitchen
body:
Purpose:
Quick working doc to (1) map out where partner/cloud listing flows break for partners during publish, (2) provide a compact bank of copy snippets for tiles, descriptions, and CTA variants, and (3) list candidate acceptance gates + QA checks for launch. Use as source of truth for the next 2-week sprint when working with partner engineering and marketplace ops.

How to use this doc:
- Product/partner PMs: pick the friction items relevant to the partner and attach screenshots.
- Solutions/SEs: copy the snippets under ‘snippet kitchen’ into partner-facing templates and adjust tone.
- Marketplace ops: follow the acceptance gates checklist during preflight and post-publish smoke tests.

FRICTION MATRIX (quick rows)
Columns: flow step | common failure mode | impact | quick mitigation | owner
1) Partner onboarding (create vendor acct) | Mismatch in legal name vs billing | Listing blocked by finance review | Add explicit naming guidance + example screenshot; surface org id earlier | GTM ops
2) Auth & SSO link (SAML/KMS) | Partner cannot provide required metadata; keys mismatch | Private deployments stalled | Provide downloadable sample metadata, template curl to validate, optional “skip for now” path for hosted-only listings | Eng-partner integrations
3) SKU & pricing mapping | Marketplace SKU doesn't accept our per-token model (hosted) | Pricing shows as flat monthly; confuses customers | Map hosted usage to “metered unit” SKU + include pricing note in tile; provide fallback SKU for trials | Finance + Marketplace ops
4) Compliance artifacts upload | Missing SOC2 artifact or incomplete CNF | Listing delayed pending legal review | Offer temporary attestation text for beta partners; mark listing as "restricted" until docs are uploaded | Legal
5) Tiles & screenshots | Asset aspect ratio or size mismatch leading to auto-crop | Low conversion on listing due to unreadable screenshot | Provide specific export presets, sample thumbnails; run automated preview before submit | Design ops
6) Integration test (API keys/endpoint) | Endpoint network restrictions (VPC) prevents marketplace test harness | Failed staging tests | Provide sample test harness that runs from partner network; allow manual verification step by SE | Eng-Solutions

SNIPPET KITCHEN (copy options)
- Short tile (28 chars max):
  1) "Redwood Inference — Fast LLM API"
  2) "Low-latency LLM serving (hosted)"
  3) "Predictable LLM inference — Redwood"

- Tagline (50–90 chars):
  1) "High-throughput, production-ready LLM inference with predictable cost and latency."
  2) "Unified runtime for hosted, dedicated, and private LLM deployments with observability."

- Long description (one paragraph):
  "Redwood Inference provides a developer-first runtime for production LLM inference. Ship with confidence using hosted APIs, reserved dedicated capacity, or private VPC deployments. Built-in routing, KV caching, and quantization recommendations help you reduce per-token cost while maintaining latency SLOs and output quality. Ideal for teams that need predictable economics and enterprise-grade controls."

- Feature bullets (short):
  - "Hosted API: simple REST/SDK for generation, chat, and embeddings"
  - "Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with SLA-backed throughput"
  - "Private: VPC & on-prem options with KMS integrations"
  - "Optimize: batching, caching, and quantization suggestions to cut unit cost"

- CTAs (variants):
  - Primary: "Start free trial"
  - Secondary: "Request dedicated capacity"
  - Enterprise: "Contact sales for private deployment"

Tone notes for partner copy: concise, developer-forward, avoid marketing hyperbole (no "magic", "revolutionary"). For enterprise partners emphasize security, SLA, and integration support. For platform partners emphasize SKU clarity and test harness availability.

ACCEPTANCE GATES (preflight checklist)
- [ ] Listing metadata complete: title, tagline, category, contact email
- [ ] Legal docs attached or attestation present (SOC2 / ISO statement)
- [ ] Pricing SKU mapped and validated with finance
- [ ] Thumbnail + banner images pass visual preview (no cropped text)
- [ ] Integration test scripts run in staging (pass) or manual verification scheduled
- [ ] Support flow documented (onboarding playbook + escalation path)
- [ ] Terms & privacy link checked and reachable
- [ ] E2E purchase/trial flow exercised (billing sandbox)

QA SMOKE TESTS (post-publish)
- Verify listing appears in search for target keywords (LLM, inference, embeddings)
- Trigger free trial signup: confirm provisioning hook & email receipt
- Run sample inference using marketplace-provided API key: check latency and token billing telemetry in console
- Attempt a region failover test (if partner supports multi-region)

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED
- Do we allow partners to publish a “hosted-only” tile that omits Dedicated/Private options? (Pros: faster publish; Cons: customer confusion)
- Billing mapping: should we present per-token pricing as tiers or as metered units? Need finance input by Nov 15.
- Will marketplace support SSO metadata upload for private deployments or do we require an SE-run setup?

NEXT STEPS (who does what)
- Marta: assemble asset export presets and upload to repo (due 2024-11-15)
- Aisha: draft partner-facing publish checklist email and attach snippet bank (due 2024-11-12)
- Eng-partner team: produce sample staging harness and CI smoke test docs (JIRA-ENG-1427)
- Noah: run through acceptance gates with first beta partner (target publish 2024-11-30)

NOTES TO SELF
- Keep snippet bank small and opinionated; marketplaces prefer clarity over long prose.
- Save one tile variation that explicitly includes "SLA" for enterprise channels.
- Add screenshot of billing mapping to avoid repeated finance questions.

Revision log:
- 2024-11-08: initial draft (Liam)
- 2024-11-15: added friction rows for compliance & SKU mapping (Marta)
- 2024-11-22: updated CTAs and next steps after SE sync (Aisha)

Attachments to add to final: export presets, sample metadata XML, billing mapping diagram, staging harness README.
